FTR Homework #9: Just got the time to post a continuation of FTR homeworks until it becomes 2nd nature. I've added PAZs and new PAZs that formed after the creation of new FTRs. I have also included DP in the analysis to see their significance.

Over the past few days, I've been repeatedly watching thevideo on decisionsand fakeout. I've also been asking and thinking to myself about what is the meaning of real PA, i.e. engulf. The real question I'm trying to answer is:Is real PA the engulf of a DP or an FTR after the DP? With more proper reading, I think I will find the answer. My best guess: FL section? still not touching that since FTRs are not done yet.

From the video, what I understand is that markets are made up of decisions about price, whether it is too cheap or expensive. These can be seen in a chart in the form of strong, well-defined DBR/RBD before the engulf of something significant on the left. The significant point of interest is another well-defined RBD/DBR, which represents another decision, etc etc etc. All chart is, therefore, drawing alternating indecisions and decisions. I believe that us RTMers, call indecisions "Flags" and decisions "Poles". Between the poles and the flags, there are set boundaries that are called flag limits, and these are the only ones we should be trading from.

Did I get that idea right? or is that just pure hallucination? As always, please do correct me if I'm getting the wrong ideas.

After this will be another FTR homework, then I'm going to finish up the non-subjective, easier to spot homeworks first such as the QM, DM and 3- drive. Only after finishing those that I'll be touching FTRs, PAZs, and eventually the FL.

Some beautifully explained charts that I found in Josh1125's journal. Thank you for these charts, Rdk123 (dunno if you're back here again or not)

Thank you for everyone contributing to this community. I learned a LOT from all of you by reading your posts and homeworks More reading, and reading, and reading, some more video time, then more reading,......

author: Frosty
text:
FTR Homework #10: Another FTR homework and what I think I have learned more about is that FTRs that gets tested and bounced more than a few times are places where ITs are either buying or selling. When these FTRs are engulfed, price then will try to reach the target, which, in my current opinion & understanding, the next origin of a move on the opposite side. For example, an FTR where price bounced down (short) from a few times, when engulfed, will create an FTR and now this FTR will become the new place where the ITs will load up on longs until the most extreme sets of orders in the next origin of move on the previous down leg has been touched. The logic applies in reverse for shorts.

From the 3 charts from FTR homework #9, I learned that the target for long orders are short orders, and vice versa. After much thinking then the extreme sets of clean orders in the origin DBR/RBD of the previous move up or down must have been the target because this is where the ITs started either buying or selling, i.e. shows their decision. This extreme sets of orders, I believe, is the MPL, which can be seen as a QM level that has not been touched yet.

Bro Staurum actually pointed this out on the CHF/JPY chart onpost #29 marked with "g". When there is no more orders left there, a new set of orders is coming in.

As for now, I will leave FTRs for a moment while finishing up on other homeworks first. Thank you all for your continuous guidance, especially fellow countryman, bro Staurum

QM Homework #1 - 3: Its time to finish up on a more objective, easier to define puzzle piece before going back to FTRs.

After reading up on QMs and after reading many QM-related posts, I have learned a few things: 1. QMs must occur at HTF important zones for them to be considered tradeable. No zone, no QM (even if it looks like one)

2. Ignored left shoulder (LS) level are a good place for a bounce on the way back.

3. QMs can work after a long period of time, not just the ones from recent past.

4. The HH or LL of QMs can be breached after creating LL or HH respectively before continuing in the QM original direction to form a diamond setup. 5. QM right shoulder need not be to the pip with the LS level. From what I understand, we should trade within the LS kink.

Regarding QM: I would think that QM is a more complex subject, and for me personally FTR leads to FL and PAZ. In all the videos, FTRs and FLs are mostly the focus.

QM is about engulf, pick up orders, and target. All these are pretty much based on FTRs and FLs.

Your markings on the charts are very simple, H,L,HH,LL or vice versa.
